text: Alpha Group phishing campaign. Victims receive a lure document that drops a loader from hxxp://update-check[.]example[.]com/stage1.bin. The loader contacts the C2 server at 203.0.113.45 over HTTPS. Observed sample SHA-256: 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08. The actors exploited CVE-2023-23397 for initial access and used PowerShell (T1059.001) for execution.

Follow-up on Alpha Group activity. A newly observed staging domain cdn-sync[.]example[.]net resolves to 198.51.100.23. The MD5 of the dropper is d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e. Operators sent spearphishing attachments (T1566.001) and beaconed over web protocols (T1071.001). The address abuse@cdn-sync[.]example[.]net was listed in the WHOIS record.

Beta crew ransomware intrusion. Initial access came through an internet-facing server vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228 and CVE-2022-30190. The attacker staged tools on 192.0.2.88 and 192.0.2.89 and exfiltrated data to login-portal.example.org. The ransom note is dropped as README.txt. Sample SHA-1: da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709. Credential dumping (T1003.001) preceded lateral movement.
Brief note: Beta crew was also seen using 192.0.2.88 for scanning. Sinkholed lookups for login-portal.example.org dropped after the takedown. No new hashes were available at publication.

Gamma operators distribute a trojanized installer from https://downloads.example.com/setup.exe. Researchers sinkholed 10.0.0.5, an internal address that appears in logs and is not an indicator. The installer's SHA-256 is e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 and it queries the C2 domain gamma-c2.example.com. Persistence is achieved via a scheduled task (T1053.005).

Delta actors target energy firms. Emails originate from billing@invoice-mail.example.com with attachments exploiting CVE-2017-11882. The second stage is fetched from 2001:db8::1 and from hxxps://files-delta[.]example[.]org/p.dll. Observed techniques: T1204.002 (user execution) and T1105 (ingress tool transfer).

Epsilon operators abused legitimate services such as docs.google.com, which is not an indicator, to host lures. The malicious payload URL was http://payload-host.example.net/a?id=7 and the payload SHA-256 is 3a7bd3e2360a3d29eea436fcfb7e44c735d117c42d1c1835420b6b9942dd4f1b.

Zeta group continues to conduct espionage against regional governments. Analysts assess with moderate confidence that the activity will persist through the next quarter. The tool, version 3.2.1.7, was not recovered. No technical indicators are included in this advisory.
